mstts:express-as.prosody: Chapter 15. Women Among the Apostles: Hidden Strength. When you think about the twelve apostles, you probably picture a group of men whose names are listed over and over. But if you look a little closer, you’ll see the early movement was actually shaped by a remarkable group of women, too. Names like Mary Magdalene, Joanna, and Salome might show up quietly in the story, but their impact was anything but small. These women were witnesses, supporters, and sometimes even leaders in their own right. Mary Magdalene, especially, stands out. She was the very first to witness the resurrection—and the first to share that life-changing news with others. Her courage, loyalty, and deep faith set an example for everyone who came after her. And even though they often worked behind the scenes, these women made all the difference. They opened their homes, shared their resources, and offered encouragement when it was needed most. Sure, they faced plenty of challenges—being overlooked, dealing with danger, and working within the limits of their time. But they never backed down. They kept going, quietly shaping the community in ways we still feel today. It’s easy to miss the people who don’t quite fit the usual mold. But the stories of these women remind us that leadership doesn’t always look the same—and that every single voice truly matters. So, if you’ve ever felt sidelined or underestimated, take heart in their example. The movement was never about just a handful of people—it’s always been a community built by many, each one bringing their own hidden strength.
